formHelp.class: isiXhosa sorts nouns into numbered classes by how they begin. The class decides the plural and every small piece in a sentence that agrees with the noun. Each card names its word’s class.
formHelp.plural: The whole word for more than one. In isiXhosa the beginning of the word changes, not the end. Write the full word.
formHelp.singular: The whole word for one. The card shows a word that is already plural; write its singular, the other half of the pair. In isiXhosa the beginning of the word changes, not the end.
formHelp.subject_concord: The small part at the start of a verb that changes with the noun doing it: “The tree is falling” and “The trees are falling” differ there. Write only that part, with a hyphen after it: xx-.
formHelp.object_concord: The small part inside a verb that changes with the noun it is done to, as in “I see the tree” and “I see the trees”. Write only that part, with a hyphen on both sides: -xx-.
formHelp.possessive: The small linking part in “the child’s tree” that changes with the thing owned (the tree), not with the owner. Write only that part, with a hyphen after it: xx-.
formHelp.locative: The word for “at, in, on, to or from” the place, thing or person: one whole word, as you would say it. Many nouns change at the start and take an ending; words like umama take a different beginning instead.

goldens.pairIntro: A noun in class {{singular}} makes its plural in class {{plural}}, and a noun in class {{plural}} is the plural of one in class {{singular}}. Each card shows one side of the pair and asks for the other.
goldens.locativeTitle: Locatives: at, in, on, to or from
goldens.locativeIntro: Each card shows a noun. Write the one word that means at, in, to or from it, as you would say it.
goldens.oldCard: On the old card, which asked for the plural of this plural, you wrote: {{form}}
goldens.earlierTitle: Earlier answers to cards no longer asked
goldens.earlierHelp: These cards asked for the plural of a word that is already plural, or of isiXhosa, which has none. They are kept here and on the server; nothing you wrote is lost, and nothing here is used.

frames.preview: Preview for admins: the sentence frames below are switched off for editors until the operator turns them on.
frames.parkedTitle: Agreement between words: coming soon, in a session together
frames.parkedBody: The questions about agreement (the small parts of a sentence that change with the noun) are being rebuilt as whole sentences to say, for a session together with the tutor. Until then they are switched off, and nothing here needs doing.
frames.example: In English, “The tree is falling” becomes “The trees are falling”: the verb changes with the noun. In isiXhosa the beginning of the verb changes with the noun’s class, and so do other small parts of the sentence: in “I see the tree”, and in “the child’s tree”. A card will show a sentence like that in English. You say it in isiXhosa, write the whole sentence, and mark the part that changed with the noun.
frames.earlierTitle: Your earlier answers to the agreement cards
frames.earlierHelp: Kept on the server, as you wrote them; nothing is lost, and nothing here is used until the new cards are on.
frames.intro: Say this in isiXhosa, as you would say it:
frames.noFrame: Write a short sentence with this word, as you would say it.
frames.anyVerb: If “falling” does not fit this word, use any verb that does. What matters is the part that changes with the noun.
frames.mark: Mark the part that agrees with the noun
frames.markHint: Select that part in the sentence above, then press the button.

clicks.title: Meet the clicks
clicks.body: isiXhosa has 15 click sounds, all built on three basic clicks: c, x and q. Tap each one to see how it is made.
clicks.c: Tongue tip behind the top teeth, pull it down sharply, like a soft 'tsk'.
clicks.x: Tongue against the side teeth, pull it away: the sound you make to a horse.
clicks.q: Tongue tip on the roof of the mouth, drop it: a hollow 'pop'.
clicks.label: The {{click}} click

hero.title: Molo!

why.title: Why isiXhosa?
why.body: A language ten million people wake up to.

speakers.title: first-language speakers
speakers.body: The second most spoken home language in South Africa, and the voice of the Eastern Cape.

official.title: official languages
official.body: Official across South Africa, and one of the three official languages of the Western Cape, Cape Town included.

clicks.title: three basic clicks, 15 click sounds
clicks.body: About one in ten everyday words has a click, a sound isiXhosa took on from its Khoekhoe and San neighbours centuries ago.

famous.title: you have heard it already
famous.body: Miriam Makeba's Click Song, the language of Wakanda in Black Panther, the home language of Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu.

why.source: Speaker numbers: Statistics South Africa, Census 2022.

voices.title: A real voice on every word
voices.body: No synthetic speech. Every word and phrase you learn was recorded by an isiXhosa speaker or comes from a licensed recording.

clicks.title: Clicks first, not as a footnote
clicks.body: Dedicated click drills: listen, tell them apart, record yourself and compare with the speaker.

human.title: Checked by people who speak it
human.body: Nothing reaches you before an isiXhosa editor has approved it. Grammar forms come from rules, not guesses.

play.title: Short, playful, daily
play.body: Five-minute lessons, spaced review that remembers for you, streaks, leagues and a small bird who cheers.

end.title: Say your first word today

lexicon.title: Lexicon data package
lexicon.intro: Download the published isiXhosa lexicon behind Molo, with its English and Norwegian glosses.
lexicon.attribution: Adapted from IsiXhosa.click, a student-led dictionary supported by the University of Cape Town and SADiLaR.
lexicon.changes: Our adaptations include learner-focused glosses, Norwegian translations, usage and contrastive notes, and editorial corrections. Each entry keeps its source and attribution.
lexicon.scope: The archive includes published headwords, glosses and example sentences, source information, attribution and licence files. Audio, exercises, curriculum, artwork and app code are excluded.
lexicon.empty: No headwords have been published yet. The download includes the licence and attribution files.
lexicon.unavailable: The lexicon package is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.

withdrawal.title: Right of withdrawal
withdrawal.expressStart: I expressly request that Molo Plus starts immediately, before the 14-day withdrawal period ends. If I withdraw, I will pay the proportion of the paid period already supplied.
withdrawal.how: Web purchases have a 14-day right of withdrawal. Open Settings → Molo Plus to submit a notice, or email support@hellomolo.com. Apple and Google purchases are handled by the store.
withdrawal.estimate: Estimated refund if you withdraw now: {{amount}}. We verify the payment before refunding.
withdrawal.estimateUnknown: We will calculate the refund from your payment and the period already supplied.
withdrawal.confirmBody: Submitting stops Plus access for this purchase immediately and registers your request to end the contract and refund the unused period.
withdrawal.pending: Your notice is registered and Plus access for this purchase is stopped. We will cancel renewal and process the refund manually within 14 days of your notice.
withdrawal.refunded: Your withdrawal has been processed and the refund recorded.
withdrawal.expired: The ordinary withdrawal period has ended. Contact support if your rights or purchase details need checking.
withdrawal.missing: Purchase missing, or need help? Contact
withdrawal.error: We could not register your withdrawal. Refresh the page or email support@hellomolo.com.

changeVerify.subject: Confirm your new email for Molo
changeVerify.body:
Open this link to use {{email}} for your Molo account: {{url}}

The link expires in an hour. Until you open it, your account keeps the old address. If you did not ask for this, ignore this email.

changeNotice.subject: Your Molo email is being changed
changeNotice.body:
Someone signed in to your Molo account asked to change its email to {{email}}. It changes only when the link sent to that address is opened.

If this was you, there is nothing to do. If it was not, sign in, change your password, and write to support@hellomolo.com.
